scenes.narration: [serious] Fake job offers targeted the builders of a missile shield.
In 2016 and 2017, emails hit U.S. defense contractors, including Lockheed Martin. Lockheed leads THAAD, a missile shield in South Korea.

visuals.at: a missile shield in South Korea

scenes.narration: The hackers studied employees on social media. Then they posed as recruiters from rival firms.
Some emails even mentioned THAAD. The bait hid malware, a hidden program.
The fake recruiters reused aliases from the Sony hack. Some logins came from North Korea.

visuals.at: reused aliases from the Sony hack

scenes.narration: In 2018, U.S. prosecutors charged a North Korean programmer. The dream job was the trap.

facts.claim: In 2016 and 2017 the conspiracy targeted several U.S. defense contractors, including Lockheed Martin, with spear-phishing emails often sent from accounts posing as recruiters at competing defense firms; some referenced THAAD, deployed in South Korea
Lockheed Martin, the prime contractor for THAAD, was not successfully infiltrated
Some messages used aliases and accounts seen in the Sony attack, sometimes accessed from North Korean IP addresses, and malware with the same data table
Before attacks, the hackers researched targets online and on social media, including Lockheed Martin employees
The attempts to infiltrate Lockheed were unsuccessful; the emails posed as recruiters at competing contractors
North Korean programmer Park Jin Hyok was charged in a complaint filed June 8, 2018 and unsealed September 6, 2018

seo.title: THAAD Phishing: Fake Recruiters Targeted Lockheed Martin Staff
